components.name: Château Gloria
components.explain:
Château Gloria is a Saint-Julien estate that Henri Martin put together from 1942, buying parcels of vines from the classed growths around it. Because it came together long after 1855, it stands outside the classification, though its vines once belonged to classed growths. Château Saint-Pierre is its sister estate.

Cabernet Sauvignon leads, with Merlot, Petit Verdot and a little Cabernet Franc; the 2017 spent 14 months in French oak. The wine is Saint-Julien in style: cassis, cedar and fine, balanced tannin.

On our list are two vintages at one price, the 2017 and the 2021. The 2017, with nine years in bottle, is the one carded to open tonight. Say: a Saint-Julien built from classed growth vines.

card.front: Why is Château Gloria not a classed growth?
card.back: It was put together from 1942 by Henri Martin out of parcels bought from Saint-Julien's classed growths, long after the 1855 classification was drawn up.

components.name: Château La Tour de Mons
components.explain:
Château La Tour de Mons is an old estate at Soussans, on the northern edge of the Margaux appellation. It takes its name from Pierre de Mons, who came to own it in 1623, and it is not one of the 1855 classed growths.

Unusually for the Médoc, Merlot leads the blend, with Cabernet Sauvignon and a little Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot: the 2020 is 57 percent Merlot. That is why it is soft and round, with plum, cassis and the rose petal perfume of Margaux.

On our list it is the 2020 at $110, the Margaux to open with the lamb shank. Say: Margaux led by Merlot, from Soussans.

card.front: What leads the blend at La Tour de Mons, and where is it?
card.back: Merlot, 57 percent in 2020, with Cabernet Sauvignon. It is at Soussans, on the northern edge of Margaux, named for Pierre de Mons, owner from 1623.

components.name: Château Charmail
components.explain:
Château Charmail is a Haut-Médoc estate at Saint-Seurin-de-Cadourne, just north of Saint-Estèphe near the Gironde. Its vineyard lies in one block, facing Château Sociando-Mallet across the road.

Charmail is known in the Médoc for cold soaking its grapes before fermentation: the chilled grapes give up color and fruit before the yeast starts, and the wine has soft tannin. Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon lead, with a good share of Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot, and the wine is aged about a year in oak, about a third of it new.

On our list it is the 2020 in magnum, printed under Large Formats and again under Bordeaux. Say: soft, generous claret for a big table.

card.front: What is Château Charmail known for in the cellar?
card.back: Cold soaking its grapes before fermentation, for color, fruit and soft tannin. It is a Haut-Médoc estate facing Sociando-Mallet across the road, north of Saint-Estèphe.
